title: Client-side beacon batcher for low-overhead tracing
creator: Maya Singh
description: Implement a lightweight client-side beacon batcher in Redwood SDKs to reduce tail latency amplification and per-request overhead from synchronous span export. The beacon batcher collects low-priority spans and non-critical telemetry, buffers them in-process with bounded memory, optionally compresses and encrypts payloads, and ships them asynchronously to the telemetry ingestion pipeline. The goal is to reduce token-serving latency amplification at p95/p99 for high-throughput clients while preserving observability for debugging and SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (node/python/go) expose opt-in 'beacon' integration with sane defaults (batch size, flush interval, max queue bytes)
End-to-end telemetry shows >=40% reduction in synchronous span export calls under our synthetic load for typical web request workloads
No increase in peak memory >5% for medium and large workloads (validated by load tests)
Beacons encrypted in transit (TLS) and optionally payload-level encrypted using customer KMS when configured
Feature gated and defaulted off for Dedicated/Private customers until rollout policy completes
Comprehensive unit + e2e tests and benchmark harness are merged
Observability: new dashboard showing beacon queue length, dropped-beacons, flush latency, and last-success-per-sdk-version
tasks: Design API shape for beaconer in SDKs (constructor options, disable hooks, telemetry tags)
Implement in JS SDK: background worker, exponential backoff, bounded queue, LRU drop strategy
Port implementation to Python and Go SDKs with consistent config semantics
Add server-side ingestion endpoint for batched beacons (ingest-proxy change) and schema migration
Write load tests comparing sync vs beacon mode across typical request shapes
Create console dashboard and alerts for 'beacon-drop-rate' and 'beacon-flush-failure-rate'
Security review and threat model (PII stripping, encryption-at-rest/transit, replay protection)
Rollout plan: opt-in beta -> default-on for non-enterprise -> opt-out flag for Dedicated/Private
